pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Harvesters — a wide field of ripe gold wheat stands half cut into stooks with reapers still bent at work away in the distance while a dozen harvest workers rest in the shade of a pear tree eating bread and porridge, after this, the lord appointed seventy-two others and sent them two by two ahead of him to every town and place he was about to visit, and he told them, the harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few, ask the lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into his harvest

pictures.scene: Mauve, Shepherdess with a Flock of Sheep — a shepherdess in a white cap and a long dark skirt leans on her crook at the edge of a misty orchard with her dog pressed close at her side while the whole flock crowds past her through the wet grass, go, i am sending you out like lambs among wolves, carry no purse or bag or sandals, do not greet anyone along the road

pictures.scene: Ostade, The Cottage Dooryard — an old woman in a white cap sits paring food at the open door of a thatched cottage hung all over with white blossom while a man leans in the doorway behind her and two small children play with a dog out in the sunlit yard, whatever house you enter, begin by saying, peace to this house, if a man of peace is there, your peace will rest on him, if not, it will return to you
pictures.name: pd_ostade_dooryard

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Supper at Emmaus — Christ sits at a plain white clothed table in a dim vaulted room breaking a small loaf in His hands with a faint light rising all round His head while one guest stares at Him in astonishment and a serving boy carries in the dish, stay at the same house, eating and drinking whatever you are offered, for the worker is worthy of his wages, do not move around from house to house, if you enter a town and they welcome you, eat whatever is set before you

pictures.scene: Ancher, The Sick Girl — a young woman propped up on blue pillows in a white bed in a bare panelled room holds a black bound book loosely in one hand and looks away past it with a small posy of red and yellow flowers set on the table at her side, heal the sick who are there and tell them, the kingdom of god is near you, but if you enter a town and they do not welcome you, go into the streets and declare
pictures.name: pd_ancher_ziekbed

pictures.scene: Martin, The Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah — a whole city burns under a vast arch of falling fire that fills the sky and tears the towers down in pieces while one tiny white robed figure hurries away along the dark ridge in the foreground, even the dust of your town that clings to our feet, we wipe off as a testimony against you, yet be sure of this, the kingdom of god is near, i tell you, it will be more bearable on that day for sodom than for that town
pictures.name: pd_martin_the_destruction_of_sodom_and_gomorrah

pictures.scene: Bendemann, The Mourning Jews in Exile — an old man in a dull red robe with an iron chain locked on his wrist sits on the ground under a vine and lets his harp lie silent across his knees while a young woman buries her face in her own arm against his side, woe to you, chorazin, woe to you, bethsaida, for if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in tyre and sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes, but it will be more bearable for tyre and sidon at the judgment than for you
pictures.name: pd_bendemann_jews_mourning_in_exile

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Tower of Babel — an enormous unfinished tower of pale stone and red brick climbs ring upon ring up into the clouds with cranes and scaffolding still standing on its topmost storeys while stonecutters work at great blocks on the grass below, and you, capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven, no, you will be brought down to hades, whoever listens to you listens to me, whoever rejects you rejects me, and whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_tower_of_babel

pictures.scene: Francisque Millet, Mountain Landscape with Lightning — a single bright bolt falls straight out of a black storm cloud down the middle of the sky over a wide dark valley of woods and small roofs while two travellers seated on the near slope point up at it, the seventy-two returned with joy and said, lord, even the demons submit to us in your name, so he told them, i saw satan fall like lightning from heaven
pictures.name: pd_francisque_millet_berglandschap_met_bliksem

pictures.scene: Raphael, Saint George and the Dragon — a knight in dark polished armour on a white horse drives his lance down into a scaly dragon that lies crushed under the horse's hooves with its wings bent and its claws splayed out flat on the bare ground, behold, i have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, nothing will harm you, nevertheless, do not rejoice that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven
pictures.name: pd_raphael_saint_george_and_the_dragon

pictures.scene: De Wet, Christ Blessing the Children — Christ sits on a low step in a dim pillared hall with a soft ring of light round His head and His hand laid on His breast while mothers press their small children in toward Him from every side and one little boy kneels at His feet, at that time jesus rejoiced in the holy spirit and declared, i praise you, father, lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children, yes, father, for this was well-pleasing in your sight, all things have been entrusted to me by my father, no one knows who the son is except the father, and no one knows who the father is except the son and those to whom the son chooses to reveal him
pictures.name: pd_dewet_christus_zegent_kinderen

pictures.scene: Guercino, King David — a bearded king wearing a small crown set over a white turban sits back in a heavy chair in a rose and gold robe lined with ermine, holding his sceptre loosely in one hand and laying the other on a great stone tablet cut with the words of his own psalm, then jesus turned to the disciples and said privately, blessed are the eyes that see what you see, for i tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it
pictures.name: pd_guercino_king_david

pictures.scene: Hart, The Rejoicing of the Law — men in long coats and striped prayer shawls carry the dressed scrolls of the law in their arms across a vaulted synagogue hung with silver lamps while the women lean over the gallery rail above them, one day an expert in the law stood up to test him, teacher, he asked, what must i do to inherit eternal life, what is written in the law, jesus replied, how do you read it
pictures.name: pd_hart_rejoicing_of_the_law

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Moses with the Tablets of the Law — an old prophet in a pale robe lifts the two dark stone tablets of the commandments high above his head with both arms, the Hebrew letters cut deep into them and catching the light, he answered, love the lord your god with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind and love your neighbor as yourself, you have answered correctly, jesus said, do this and you will live
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_moses_with_the_tablets_of_the_law

pictures.scene: Rosa, Bandits on a Rocky Coast — a band of armed men in ragged tunics and feathered caps waits on a bare rock above a lonely road at evening with pikes and a long staff propped beside them while one of them points away down the hill, but wanting to justify himself, he asked jesus, and who is my neighbor, jesus took up this question and said, a man was going down from jerusalem to jericho when he fell into the hands of robbers, they stripped him, beat him, and went away, leaving him half dead
pictures.name: pd_rosa_bandits_on_a_rocky_coast

pictures.scene: Millais, Three Elders — three old bearded men in a black robe, a dull brown robe and a red one stand barefoot close together on a bare rock under a hot yellow sky, the one in the middle sunk in thought with his eyes cast down while the other two look away over his head, now by chance a priest was going down the same road, but when he saw him, he passed by on the other side, so too, when a levite came to that spot and saw him, he passed by on the other side
pictures.name: pd_millais_priesters

pictures.scene: Fetti, The Good Samaritan — a traveller in a white shirt and a crimson cloak braces himself under the weight of a wounded man and heaves him up bodily onto the back of a patient grey donkey standing on the stony road, with wind blown trees above them and the robbers still going off along the ridge behind, but when a samaritan on a journey came upon him, he looked at him and had compassion, he went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine, then he put him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him
pictures.name: pd_fetti_samaritan

pictures.scene: Isaac van Ostade, The Inn Yard — a crowded yard outside a thatched country inn where a maid carries out a stone jug to a carter resting against his load, with horses and a wagon waiting under the trees, children playing on the ground and smoke going up from the chimney, the next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper, take care of him, he said, and on my return i will repay you for any additional expense, which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers
pictures.name: pd_isaac_van_ostade_herberg

pictures.scene: Ghirlandaio, The Visitation — a young woman in a deep blue cloak bends forward under a stone arch to take an old kinswoman by the shoulders as the older woman sinks down on her knees before her in a wide gold mantle and looks up into her face, with a walled city and a river lying far off through the opening behind them, the one who showed him mercy, replied the expert in the law, then jesus told him, go and do likewise, as they traveled along, jesus entered a village where a woman named martha welcomed him into her home
pictures.name: pd_ghirlandaio_visitation

pictures.scene: Vermeer, Christ in the House of Martha and Mary — Christ sits back in a purple tunic and a heavy blue mantle with His bare feet on the floor and opens His hand toward a young woman who is sitting low beside Him with her chin propped on her fist, while her sister leans across the white clothed table to set down a basket of bread and speak to Him, she had a sister named mary, who sat at the lord's feet listening to his message, but martha was distracted by all the preparations to be made, she came to jesus and said, lord, do you not care that my sister has left me to serve alone, tell her to help me
pictures.name: pd_vermeer_christ_in_the_house_of_martha_and_mary

pictures.scene: Dou, Old Woman Reading a Lectionary — an old woman in a fur trimmed dark coat and a linen headband holds a great printed gospel book open in both hands close to her face and reads it in silence out of a plain brown dark room, with the light falling only on the page and on her forehead and hands, martha, martha, the lord replied, you are worried and upset about many things, but only one thing is necessary, mary has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her
pictures.name: pd_dou_old_woman_reading_a_lectionary

lines.text: After this, the Lord appointed seventy-two others and sent them two by two ahead of Him to every town and place He was about to visit.
And He told them, The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.
Go! I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
Carry no purse or bag or sandals. Do not greet anyone along the road.
Whatever house you enter, begin by saying, Peace to this house.
If a man of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; if not, it will return to you.
Stay at the same house, eating and drinking whatever you are offered. For the worker is worthy of his wages. Do not move around from house to house.
If you enter a town and they welcome you, eat whatever is set before you.
Heal the sick who are there and tell them, The kingdom of God is near you.
But if you enter a town and they do not welcome you, go into the streets and declare,
Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet, we wipe off as a testimony against you. Yet be sure of this: The kingdom of God is near.
I tell you, it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town.
Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you.
And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades!
Whoever listens to you listens to Me; whoever rejects you rejects Me; and whoever rejects Me rejects the One who sent Me.
The seventy-two returned with joy and said, Lord, even the demons submit to us in Your name.
So He told them, I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.
Behold, I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will harm you.
Nevertheless, do not rejoice that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.

At that time Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and declared, I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.
All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, and no one knows who the Father is except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.
Then Jesus turned to the disciples and said privately, Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.
For I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.
One day an expert in the law stood up to test Him. Teacher, he asked, what must I do to inherit eternal life?
What is written in the Law? Jesus replied. How do you read it?
He answered, Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind and Love your neighbor as yourself.
You have answered correctly, Jesus said. Do this and you will live.
But wanting to justify himself, he asked Jesus, And who is my neighbor?
Jesus took up this question and said, A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho when he fell into the hands of robbers. They stripped him, beat him, and went away, leaving him half dead.
Now by chance a priest was going down the same road, but when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
So too, when a Levite came to that spot and saw him, he passed by on the other side.
But when a Samaritan on a journey came upon him, he looked at him and had compassion.
He went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. Then he put him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
The next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper. Take care of him, he said, and on my return I will repay you for any additional expense.
Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?
The one who showed him mercy, replied the expert in the law. Then Jesus told him, Go and do likewise.
As they traveled along, Jesus entered a village where a woman named Martha welcomed Him into her home.
She had a sister named Mary, who sat at the Lord's feet listening to His message.
But Martha was distracted by all the preparations to be made. She came to Jesus and said, Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me!
Martha, Martha, the Lord replied, you are worried and upset about many things.
But only one thing is necessary. Mary has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her.
